result:
**I would eliminate the instinct for dominance and "us vs. them" thinking.**

If I could change one thing about the world, it would be to remove humanity's hardwired tendency to sort ourselves into tribes, to seek power over others, and to feel pleasure in having enemies. 

Everything else—war, inequality, environmental destruction, even a lot of personal misery—flows downstream from that single ancient flaw in our operating system. We evolved in small bands where being able to quickly identify "them" and rally against them kept us alive. That same wiring now scales catastrophically in a world of 8 billion people with nuclear weapons, social media, and planetary-scale problems.

Imagine a version of humanity that still has ambition, competition, passion, and disagreement—but without the reflexive need to dehumanize the other side. We'd still argue fiercely. We'd still strive. But the argument would be about ideas and outcomes instead of identity and dominance. We'd be able to coordinate at scales we've never managed before.

Every other grand fix people dream about (ending scarcity, perfect governance, total peace, etc.) either fails or becomes dystopian without this foundational change. Give humans unlimited power and resources while keeping our current psychology and you just get more sophisticated ways to hate and dominate each other.

So yeah. One change.

**Rewire the primate brain so that status-seeking and belonging no longer require an enemy.**

The rest of the problems would still be hard. But they'd finally be solvable.
